frame: Model T-pose space of the rig: +X = character's left, +Y = up, +Z = forward. Axes are given for the LEFT side and the trunk; the right side is generated by mirroring (axial vectors: (x, y, z) -> (x, -y, -z)), so the rig is symmetric by construction.
angle_convention: Swing-twist from the joint's anatomical neutral (rest unless 'neutral' says otherwise). 'flex' and 'abd' are the swing rotation-vector components on those axes; 'twist' turns about the segment's long axis; 'twist_axis': 'distal' = the positive axis points away from the body. Positive directions are named in 'labels'.
limit_policy: soft ~ clinical active range-of-motion norms (no resistance inside); hard ~ passive end range plus a margin (the pose is never allowed beyond). Between soft and hard is the resistance zone that phase 3 will turn into progressive joint torque. Values are rounded, tunable starting points, not universal truths: ranges vary with age, sex, training and the position of neighbouring joints (e.g. hip flexion with a straight knee is limited by the hamstrings).

sources.AAOS: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (1965), Joint Motion: Method of Measuring and Recording; normative values as reproduced in Greene & Heckman (1994), The Clinical Measurement of Joint Motion, AAOS.
sources.NORKIN: Norkin C.C., White D.J., Measurement of Joint Motion: A Guide to Goniometry, 5th ed., F.A. Davis, 2016 (tables of normative values from AAOS, AMA and population studies).
sources.SOUCIE: Soucie J.M. et al. (2011), Range of motion measurements: reference values and a database for comparison studies, Haemophilia 17(3):500-507 (CDC normal joint study, 674 healthy subjects 2-69 y).
sources.WHITE_PANJABI: White A.A., Panjabi M.M., Clinical Biomechanics of the Spine, 2nd ed., Lippincott, 1990 (representative segmental ranges of motion, table of limits and representative values).
sources.LUDEWIG: Ludewig P.M. et al. (2009), Motion of the shoulder complex during multiplanar humeral elevation, J Bone Joint Surg Am 91(2):378-389 (clavicle elevation, retraction and posterior rotation with arm elevation).
sources.INMAN: Inman V.T., Saunders J.B., Abbott L.C. (1944), Observations on the function of the shoulder joint, J Bone Joint Surg 26(1):1-30 (scapulohumeral rhythm about 2:1).

Spine.notes: Sum of the five lumbar levels; axial rotation is small in the lumbar spine (facet orientation). Trunk totals (Spine+Chest+UpperChest soft): flexion 81, extension 31, lateral 39, rotation 56 vs AAOS thoracolumbar 80 / 25 / 35 / 45 (rotation kept generous: segmental thoracic values sum higher than the clinical trunk measure).

Chest.region: lower thoracic spine T7-T12 (pivot at T12/L1)
Chest.notes: Thoracolumbar transition; axial rotation per level falls from about 8 (T7-T8) to 2 degrees (T11-L1), roughly 25 per side in total.

UpperChest.region: upper thoracic spine T1-T6 with rib cage (pivot mid-thorax)
UpperChest.notes: The rib cage stiffens flexion and lateral bending; axial rotation is the largest thoracic motion (about 8-9 degrees per level per side in the upper thorax). Authored clips concentrate trunk rotation and forward lean in this bone (Quaternius Jog_Fwd: about 33 degrees of rotation with 20 of flexion), so its flexion budget is wider than the T1-T6 segmental sum (about 20).

Neck.region: lower cervical spine C2-T1 (pivot at C7/T1)
Neck.notes: Neck+Head soft totals: flexion 46, extension 58, lateral 34, rotation 67 vs AAOS cervical 45 / 55 / 45 / 70 (soft lateral kept lower: mostly lower cervical, coupled with rotation).

Head.region: upper cervical C0-C1-C2 (pivot at the atlanto-occipital joint)
Head.notes: About half of cervical axial rotation happens at C1-C2.

LeftShoulder.region: shoulder girdle: clavicle at the sternoclavicular joint (scapula follows; scapulothoracic motion is not a separate bone in the humanoid profile)
LeftShoulder.notes: Design: a scapulohumeral rhythm driver (phase 2) will add girdle elevation / posterior rotation as a function of humeral elevation (about 1 degree of girdle per 2 of glenohumeral motion above 30 degrees). Authored clips may already animate this bone.

LeftUpperArm.region: shoulder: glenohumeral joint (limits are for the whole shoulder complex, see notes)

neutral.meaning: arm hanging at the side (anatomical neutral); the T-pose rest is 90 degrees of abduction

LeftUpperArm.notes: AAOS: flexion 180, extension 60, abduction 180, internal rotation 70, external 90. Authored clips usually carry most arm elevation on this bone, so it holds the whole complex's range; capped at 178 to stay clear of the swing-twist singularity at 180 (arm straight overhead remains reachable for hanging). The elliptical swing cone is an approximation of the real (non-elliptical) humeral cone; adduction at zero flexion is really limited by the torso, which is a collision, not a joint limit.

LeftLowerArm.notes: AAOS: flexion 150, pronation 80, supination 80. The palms-down T-pose is forearm neutral (thumb forward), so rest = 0. Up to about 10 degrees of hyperextension is common (more in women).

LeftHand.notes: AAOS: flexion 80, extension 70, radial 20, ulnar 30. Forearm pronation belongs to LowerArm; clips that put it on the hand bone will show as wrist twist violations (reported by the retarget test).

LeftUpperLeg.notes: AAOS: flexion 120, extension 30, abduction 45, adduction 30, internal and external rotation 45. Flexion with a straight knee is limited to about 90 by the hamstrings (two-joint coupling; phase 2/3).

LeftLowerLeg.notes: AAOS: flexion 135, extension 0. Tibial rotation is near zero at full extension (screw-home) and grows with flexion; phase 1 uses a constant range.

LeftFoot.notes: AAOS: dorsiflexion 20, plantarflexion 50, inversion 35, eversion 15. The foot bone's long axis runs from the ankle to the ball of the foot.

LeftToes.region: metatarsophalangeal joints (one bone for all toes)
LeftToes.notes: AAOS first MTP: extension 70, flexion 45. Toe-off in running uses 50-60 degrees of extension.

dynamics_placeholder: Each joint will gain {stiffness, damping, max_torque_nm, rest_tension} in phase 3; they are intentionally absent until they are measured against the physics prototype.
